intent: Improve precise, strong musical impacts and the overall automatic ride while preserving authored inputs, impact definitions, seeded geometry plans, normal lines, and the prior dashboard. Numerical gains alone are insufficient.

experiments.result: 24/24 baseline tracks and physics counts exactly reproduce s3-c.

experiments.hypothesis: Use the remainder of the pair-refinement allowance on measured-sensitive coordinate blocks instead of leaving it unused.
experiments.interpretation: Mixed generalization within the dev panel; better perturbed strength with more body dragging and worse authored strength. Extra local descent does not reliably improve the complete ride.

experiments.hypothesis: At the same nominal evaluation allowance, transfer up to 24 initial-proposal samples to continuation guidance, enabling a response step and spending leftover rounds on coordinates.
experiments.interpretation: Reducing proposal breadth to fund local continuation refinement hurt the strongest impacts; a fairer nominal allocation was not a better physical allocation.

experiments.hypothesis: Kinematic catch-incidence proposals may find stronger, cleaner hits than shallow inherited entry proposals. Same full allowance and guards.
experiments.interpretation: Sharper entry candidates did not deliver a convincing quality gain and increased dragging and awkward arrivals. Entry sharpness alone is insufficient.

experiments.hypothesis: The future-value predictor ignores requested constructions and has historical evaluation-song overlap. Recollect current compiler probes on disjoint source groups and compare geometry-conditioned prediction, same-data geometry-blind prediction, and deletion.
experiments.interpretation: Better held-group prediction is not a consistent complete-ride gain. Geometry conditioning improves perturbed mean loss but weakens its very strongest hits and increases authored head-down arrivals. Test whether local optimization is the wrong role for a tree predictor before deciding its value.

experiments.hypothesis: Replace strong-arrival absolute heading/total-speed priors with normal/tangential centre velocity in the sled frame. Unlike the previous extra pose penalty, replace the competing constraints rather than adding one.
experiments.interpretation: The posture guard improves substantially, but real impacts and speed tracking worsen. A lower guard count is not sufficient.

experiments.hypothesis: Rebase response corrections at the best finite-difference probe, keeping the Jacobian, allowance and actual acceptance checks.
experiments.interpretation: Mixed small changes; rebasing does not reliably improve complete rides. Pair-response tests pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Complete-track refinement may stall because changed geometry invalidates saved suffix controls. Compare fixed rebuilding with bounded local repair only on those failures, on the same four saved seed-101 tracks. Every replacement must improve the complete objective.
experiments.caveat: Four-case feasibility study with extra work, not a production-panel gain.
experiments.result: Initial local-only rescue had no valid anchor and could not explore. Corrected seeded rescue recovered 1,637/1,823 invalid intervals, but only one of four rides improved, by 0.000059 whole-objective loss, for about 1M extra frames each.

experiments.hypothesis: Reassess deletion of the old future model under current construction policies; comparator for disjoint replacements.
experiments.status: candidate for simplification, not yet selected
experiments.interpretation: Impact quality is broadly similar, but air error and body dragging rise. Await the disjoint model comparisons.

experiments.hypothesis: Preserve suffix shape by rigid translation instead of reconstructing its controls, then validate complete physical behavior.
experiments.result: 0 improvements in four saved rides; most candidates still fail downstream construction or survival. Preserving drawn geometry does not preserve the rider state.

experiments.hypothesis: Trade two-branch depth-two continuation for single-branch depth-three continuation at comparable tree work, retaining root diversity.
experiments.interpretation: The depth-for-branching trade worsens authored strength and air tracking, with mixed perturbed results.

experiments.hypothesis: Keep a curve’s segment count fixed at its nominal duration during duration refinement to remove one source of discontinuous response. Preserve explicit faceted styles.
experiments.baselineCheck: Shared geometry source affects the evaluator fingerprint; all 24 baseline tracks were explicitly remeasured and every measured result is exactly unchanged.
experiments.interpretation: No convincing complete-ride improvement; quiet strength bias and air error increase. The geometry-sharing identity was explicitly remeasured, with exact unchanged baseline measurements.

experiments.hypothesis: Use unused response-round samples for differences between viable controls with the same topology, giving joint directions derived from measured feasible geometry.
experiments.interpretation: Small mean loss gains coexist with weaker very strong impacts, more dragging on perturbations and greater authored burst excess. Not adopted.

experiments.hypothesis: Shrink the response trust radius when the response step itself fails, even if coordinate probes improved the candidate.
experiments.interpretation: Shrinking after failed joint steps does not improve the complete authored rides; quiet strength rises above request.

experiments.hypothesis: Prepare steeper downward arrivals before strong asks, keeping the existing speed target, upright constraint and actual continuation judge.
experiments.interpretation: Very strong hits improve, but body dragging rises by roughly 1.1–1.5 seconds per minute and older impact rulers worsen. This is a physical tradeoff, not an unqualified gain.

experiments.hypothesis: Retain the selected two-interval continuation during joint refinement and use the same leaf valuation.
experiments.interpretation: The first coherent-horizon trial weakens very strong hits and increases authored impact loss. Keep the underlying horizon mismatch under investigation rather than adopt this execution.

experiments.hypothesis: Retain four distinct, physically replayed scattered arrivals for continuation search instead of the first viable carrier reconstruction.
experiments.interpretation: 48/48 dev and confirmation rides complete and fulfill their fixed plans. Mean impact loss improves in all four subsets; very-strong authored confirmation bias worsens by 0.011. Eight paired clips retain improvements, random strong beats and the worst regression. No product promotion yet.

experiments.hypothesis: Characterize local catch capacity from exact saved prefixes at larger local allowance.
experiments.result: All 179 strong-request saved impacts reproduce exactly across four seed-101 rides. Extra local search improves mean strength bias by 0.007–0.015 per song, before testing any continuation. Two scattered searches lose a previously verified valid construction; these are independently reproduced and investigated in Q19.
experiments.caveat: Extra work and fixed-prefix local outcomes, not improved complete tracks.

experiments.hypothesis: Broader one-interval physical screening followed by deeper continuation of promising roots, at comparable approximate tree work and unchanged total allowance.
experiments.interpretation: Staged deeper selection improves mean strength but increases body dragging and authored head-down arrivals; not adopted.

experiments.hypothesis: Keep already validated scattered candidates from the exact prefix/objective memo while reconstructing new carriers.
experiments.reproduction: Q17 loses Tiki section 59 and Luna section 42. This version retains both at exactly their prior measured impacts, 0.494 and 0.708 (rounded).
experiments.interpretation: Verified fragmented incumbents are now retained in both exact reproductions. Full-track perturbed strength improves but dragging also rises; investigate the complete retention and interruption contract before promotion.
experiments.caveat: A later exact-control counterexample showed this prototype could return an unrelated cached fragment. Saved tracks remain physically measured, but the proposal contract was wrong. Q27 fixes eligible incumbent retention without admitting unrelated controls.

experiments.hypothesis: Add tangential placement of the receiving curve as an explicit geometric degree of freedom; verify unchanged baseline under the new evaluator identity.
experiments.interpretation: Fixed-prefix strength improves very slightly, but full authored impact loss and very-strong strength worsen. Extra geometric freedom is not yet useful.

experiments.hypothesis: Combine preservation of verified scattered incumbents with distinct scattered alternatives, testing the interaction explicitly.
experiments.interpretation: Perturbed loss improves, authored stays nearly unchanged; guard tradeoffs remain. Do not equate a local retention invariant with universal musical quality.
experiments.caveat: A later exact-control counterexample showed this prototype could return an unrelated cached fragment. Saved tracks remain physically measured, but the proposal contract was wrong. Q27 fixes eligible incumbent retention without admitting unrelated controls.

experiments.hypothesis: Resolve the current search profile before loading its construction policies, avoiding loading and replacing the V6 archive during V3 production.
experiments.interpretation: One coherent configuration path loads the selected archive once. All tracks, physics counts and judge results are exactly unchanged. Cold-process heap observation is not a whole-compile speed claim.

experiments.hypothesis: Separate learned arrival ranking from finite-difference geometry refinement: disable only the local learned-value residual, with both inherited and disjoint geometry-conditioned predictors.
experiments.interpretation: Removing local learned gradients is mixed alone. Geometry-aware ranking is more promising when physical alternatives survive across boundaries (Q25c).

experiments.hypothesis: Characterize the unchanged compiler on the full dev panel at six million physics frames per ride, compared with the ordinary duration-scaled allowance.
experiments.interpretation: Doubling the ceiling to six million frames only spends about 0.10–0.14 million more; local caps and retained alternatives limit useful scaling. Very-strong impact delivery gets weaker in this trial.

experiments.hypothesis: Carry four distinct physical prefixes across the song within the shared allowance rather than committing after short lookahead; final selection uses the unchanged complete-track objective.
experiments.interpretation: Persistent width-four physical prefixes improve many completed cases but fail one of 24 declared rides. Failures remain in all aggregate results.

experiments.hypothesis: Widen the persistent physical-prefix beam to eight within the same shared allowance.
experiments.interpretation: Width alone does not solve viability: two of 24 rides fail.

experiments.status: promising quality, completion failures; not adopted
experiments.hypothesis: Use a disjoint geometry-conditioned future predictor only to rank persistent physical prefixes, not as a local geometry gradient.
experiments.interpretation: 24/24 development and 24/24 earlier confirmation complete with lower impact loss and better strong delivery. A newly declared 48-case panel exposes two failures (46/48 complete). No promotion. Completed-track gains cannot excuse missing rides.
experiments.caveat: Same four songs throughout; fresh seeds are not unseen music. Any later reuse of the 48-case panel is a recheck, not independent fresh confirmation.

experiments.status: not adopted; inherits prototype exact-probe defect
experiments.hypothesis: Combine geometry-conditioned rank-only prediction with scattered retention.
experiments.interpretation: Better perturbed impact loss, but inherits Q21 exact-control contamination. Superseded by explicit eligibility in Q27.

experiments.status: complete development; tested invariant, under integration
experiments.hypothesis: Preserve a verified fragment only if its control is offered in this search; retain it across budget interruption and consider distinct carrier arrivals.
experiments.interpretation: Native fixtures reproduce lost incumbents on two actual prefixes; old code fails and corrected code passes. Exact-control probes exclude unrelated cached fragments. All 24 rides complete; impact loss improves slightly authored and more on perturbations.
experiments.validation: Two native regression fixtures cover replayed incumbent, broad search, exact-control exclusion and interruption recovery.

experiments.hypothesis: Test whether greater local impact weight alone improves complete rides under unchanged independent rulers.
experiments.interpretation: Stronger hits and lower impact loss come with worse speed, air, body dragging and extra-hit diagnostics. Not accepted as overall quality improvement.

experiments.status: confirmed accounting bug; correction under integration
experiments.hypothesis: Outgoing authored-span estimate and later replacement must use identical authored bounds and search targets, even when physical construction starts before the beat or targets are jittered.
experiments.interpretation: Frozen replay audit: all 24 old accumulated estimates disagree with complete span losses; consistent windows and targets reconcile to floating-point precision. Two native tests fail old code and pass corrected code. The corrected old search weakens very-strong hits, so test with the new architecture rather than claim automatic quality gains.
experiments.caveat: This is the internal search cost. Final independent evaluators never used these inconsistent incremental estimates.

experiments.hypothesis: Terminal candidate selection, refinement and final choice must evaluate the same whole-track objective, including support motion and engagement preferences.
experiments.interpretation: One complete-ride objective now drives terminal choice, refinement and final selection. Native regression tests fail on the old implementation. 48 paired rides show negligible quality change; 63 parity cells qualified with six deliberate hash changes, 33 judge references, 276 tests, typecheck and reachability pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Keep eight untried distinct alternatives at four recent beam boundaries; recover only after a physical dead end, within the original global allowance.
experiments.interpretation: Bounded recovery resolves both exposed failures. All 48 rides complete and satisfy construction. Authored/perturbed impact loss −0.006/−0.004, strong bias +0.014/+0.009, quiet bias −0.007/−0.003, speed error −0.005/−0.004. Body drag −0.094/+0.246 s/min; every ruler retained. Same 24 development tracks and physics counts as Q25c. This panel has now informed development and is not fresh confirmation.

experiments.hypothesis: Combine physical-prefix beam and bounded recovery with consistent authored-span accounting and eligible scattered retention. Test interactions explicitly against both baseline and Q32.
experiments.interpretation: Coherent beam plus span accounting and eligible fragments: all 24 complete; impact loss −0.005/−0.010, strong bias +0.011/+0.025, speed error −0.012/−0.010. Authored body dragging +0.685 s/min; not accepted solely on musical averages.

experiments.status: complete development, confirmation and 6M; not promoted
experiments.interpretation: Coherent shared-objective beam improves musical loss on both 24-case panels, with body dragging +0.33/+0.53 s/min in confirmation. Higher first-pass budget offers only a small gain.

experiments.hypothesis: Complete-incumbent suffix refinement with the same beam search and complete objective. Standard and 6M panels compare against unrefined coherent beam; repaired rides must never replace a better complete incumbent.
experiments.interpretation: Complete-incumbent suffix repair spends about 3.2M more physics frames at 6M allowance for a small additional musical gain; body dragging worsens. Investigating actual accepted work.

experiments.hypothesis: Ablate future prediction from coherent beam, retaining physical local costs and priors.
experiments.interpretation: Removing future prediction loses some strongest-hit delivery; no general improvement in guards.

experiments.hypothesis: Test inherited rank-only predictor in coherent beam; disclose evaluation-song overlap of old model.
experiments.interpretation: Inherited predictor has evaluation-song overlap and weaker very-strong delivery than the disjoint geometry-aware predictor; perturbed body dragging is worse.
Adding angular velocity and circular pose to arrival diversity is physically motivated but mixed, not a clear improvement.
Beam nodes now own prefix arrays, interrupted search preserves the deepest prefix, and width respects the minimum affordable local search. Native budget tests pass; dev24 nearly unchanged.
Locally fitted two-support patches usually fail to improve the complete track after continuation. Q43 tests full-ride response instead of trusting the local surrogate.

experiments.status: development, confirmation and 48-case recheck complete; candidate
experiments.interpretation: Completes all 96 tracks across three panels. Impact loss improves under v2 and v3; some independent older-ruler and body-drag measures regress. Separate clips retain strong improvements, worst regression and quiet example. Clean implementation under qualification.
Full-objective response makes small gains; telemetry shows repeated tiny improvements near the tail. No broad quality gain justifies this additional path.
Four prefixes save roughly 0.9M frames but lose much of the quality gain and increase body dragging.
Two prefixes save roughly 1.8M frames but worsen authored impact loss and strong impact delivery.
Visit high-regret supports without resetting the sweep after every tiny improvement. Tests tail starvation observed in Q43.
Restore sequential planning with consistent accounting and additive future ranking. Quality gains are weaker and perturbed body dragging rises; supports retaining multiple physical prefixes.

experiments.status: 48 development/confirmation pairs and 24 high-budget cases complete; not promoted
experiments.interpretation: Predict the existing arrival preference one frame forward instead of assessing stale boundary pose and heading. First panel reduces inverted/backward strong arrivals while improving impact error; quiet and drag tradeoffs still require confirmation.

experiments.hypothesis: One extra native step observes the incoming pose exactly. Completes dev24 and reduces some pose failures, but raises perturbed body dragging by .681 s/min; not a clear improvement over the cheaper Q48 forecast.

experiments.status: standard and high-budget panels complete; not adopted
experiments.hypothesis: Test sixteen retained physical prefixes at standard and 6M allowance, against the eight-prefix Q48 controls. Wider future diversity may make better use of extra compute than repeated tail repair.
experiments.interpretation: Sixteen prefixes at standard allowance worsens several strength results. At 6M, it improves v3 loss by .002/.003 relative to eight prefixes but spends about 2.45M more frames, raises authored inverted arrivals by .027 and increases hidden bend diagnostics. Breadth is useful but not a clear overall default improvement. The high-budget process was interrupted after 22 records and resumed under the identical frozen plan; all24 records are present.

experiments.hypothesis: Replace duplicate JS contact history with native metered contact-window replays; verify exact collisions, then compare all rulers.
experiments.interpretation: 219681 reference positions exact; 24 complete pairs show mixed quality. Long-case peak RSS 4446→4381 MiB, not a large memory reduction. Wall time 537→466 s under concurrent load is not a controlled speed claim.

experiments.hypothesis: Retain resolved contact positions in existing native collision records and construct scattered fragments from the original evaluated carrier. Remove the separate observer and observation replay. Require unchanged physical trajectories, zero additional simulation on cached reads, and complete paired quality/resource comparisons.
experiments.interpretation: Relative to Q42, v3 impact loss improves by about .001 authored/.002 perturbed; strongest authored hits improve. Older-ruler perturbed error and body dragging are mixed/worse. Pure construction now uses the original cached collision record; no separate observer history or replay. All 48 baseline/Q42 saved tracks were explicitly remeasured under the new backend identity. No promotion yet.
experiments.confirmation: All24 confirmation rides complete and fulfilled; v3 loss −.006/−.008, strong bias +.018/+.020, very strong bias +.016/+.026, quiet bias −.008/−.005 (authored/perturbed). Body drag +.276/+.323 s/min with wide four-song intervals; all rulers retained.

experiments.status: 63 exact compiler cells; integrated structural candidate
experiments.hypothesis: Native version arena slots reserve an inline large Version even when empty. Store owned version nodes behind compact optional pointers; preserve handle IDs, access order, physics and work. Require all63 exact compiler checks plus independent judging, tests and measured long-case memory/runtime.
experiments.evidence: At 50.6 s in the read-only long-case audit: version slot array 318767104 bytes, 8072 live version nodes. Array storage remains after holder reclamation.

result.caveat: Different concurrent loads; timing is exploratory and does not establish a speed gain. Pointer indirection/allocation may cost CPU. Testing direct branch reclamation next.

experiments.status: 63 exact compiler cells; long stress exact; integration checks pass
experiments.hypothesis: Reclaim released version branches as soon as neither a live descendant nor the current shared cache needs their ancestry. Keep handle slots reserved until lineage death to prevent premature reuse. Preserve physics/cache access order and work; test ownership cases, exact 63-cell parity, long-track hash/work and resource use.
experiments.evidence: Read-only audit sees millions of retained version nodes although search retains only eight prefix engines. All released versions currently remain until the entire lineage dies.

experiments.hypothesis: Combine the existing one-step arrival preference forecast with cached contact construction and the coherent beam. Compare complete paired panels under every unchanged ruler, including inverted arrivals and body dragging; neither component implies the combination is better.
experiments.interpretation: Confirmation versus original baseline: v3 impact loss −.007/−.008, strong bias +.019/+.013, very-strong +.022/+.021, quiet bias −.007/−.006, inverted/backward −.064/−.006 (authored/perturbed). Body drag +.188/+.500 s/min, older-ruler timing mixed. Compare directly against Q52 before selecting.

experiments.hypothesis: Evaluate the clean cached-contact compiler without learned future ranking, retaining native local cost and arrival preferences. This tests whether the current learned artifact earns its complexity in the actual final architecture, independently of feature-prediction accuracy. All measures and completion remain unchanged.
experiments.interpretation: Without model versus Q52: v3 loss +.001/+.002, strong bias −.006/−.009, very-strong −.008/−.009, inverted arrivals +.019/+.021, body drag +.099/+.730 s/min. The current model helps on this panel; no-model is not adopted.

experiments.hypothesis: Replace per-version heap allocations with dense owned nodes and a compact stable-handle index. Swap removal updates the moved node’s handle mapping; external handles and ancestry ownership remain unchanged. Test exact tracks/work, ownership, memory and process CPU before choosing it over the simpler boxed version arena.

Refit the 73-feature geometry-aware continuation model on 336 disjoint native probe compiles from the coherent search. Keep hyperparameters and the physical target fixed, validate held-out catalog groups and independent export predictions, then compare complete production panels against Q52 and the no-model ablation. Prediction improvements alone do not justify adoption.

Refit the 57-feature arrival-only continuation model on 336 disjoint native probe compiles from the coherent search. Keep hyperparameters and the physical target fixed, validate held-out catalog groups and independent export predictions, then compare complete production panels against Q52 and the no-model ablation. Prediction improvements alone do not justify adoption.

limitations: Four songs only; confirmation seeds do not establish unseen-music generalization.
Physical posture and body-drag diagnostics are guards and observations, not newly validated aesthetic objectives.
Compile-time differences during concurrent research jobs are confounded by machine load; physics-frame accounting is the work comparison until isolated timing checks.

diagnostics.caveat: Descriptive association across the 24-case development panel; target mix and arrival posture differ, so this does not establish a cause.

responseStudy.interpretation: Most local improvement comes from actual coordinate probes. This motivates a better use of their measured progress, not the claim that joint steps have no value.

beamPhysicalReview.scope: Five of eight clip pairs inspected frame by frame, with independent physical decomposition for all 1890 matched beats on the 24-case development panel. Owner visual approval remains open.
findings: Amour 101, 21.23 s: strength .430→.820; upright entry, travel impulse 2.98→5.92; strong catch improves physically.
Tiki 202, 13.93 s: inverted/bent landing becomes upright; travel impulse 3.31→5.20; strength .441→.695.
Amour 202, 13.90 s: worst regression .583→.242; steeply tilted entry remains, weaker travel response.
Tiki 101, 46.20 s: numerical quiet improvement .264→.110 becomes inverted head contact. This is not an acceptable example of improved smoothness.
beamPhysicalReview.guard: Do not promote on impact-error averages alone; preserve the quiet counterexample in review.

q42PhysicalReview.scope: Three selected pairs inspected frame by frame; all 1890 matched hits decomposed. Owner visual review remains open.
findings: Amour 101 8.88s: inverted baseline becomes an upright sled catch, .368 to .726; travel impulse 5.47 vs spin .39 in candidate.
Amour 202 7.90s: worst regression .827 to .419, lower normal approach speed and weaker travel response.
Tiki 303 45.33s: quieter .299 to .144 with upright entry; later guide contact still bends the rider, so this is not proof of complete calmness.
